What is Timestamp

One sentence explanation

timestamp is the version number of the ATOM diagram. The server uses it to determine whether you have the latest version of the diagram when you submit the modification.

why it is needed

A picture may be modified in multiple places at the same time:

  • The user of the front-end interface is dragging the node

  • Your script calls API at the same time to modify parameters

  • Another service is also updating this image concurrently

Without version checking, modifications submitted later will directly overwrite those submitted earlier, resulting in data loss or inconsistent graph structure.

timestamp is a monotonically increasing version number maintained by the server: every time the graph is modified, the server updates this value. When the client submits modifications, it must carry the latest timestamp it got. If it does not match the server (the description picture has been changed without your knowledge), the server will reject the submission.

SDK What is processed automatically

SDK automatically caches timestamp on the following occasions:

  • open_graph() After success

  • After successful modification operations such as create_node(), delete_node(), connect_nodes(), etc.

  • Any operation whose return value contains the timestamp field

The cache name is key, and multiple pictures are maintained independently. *Subsequent editing operations automatically carry the *cached timestamp, no manual transmission is required.

When might something go wrong again?

Even though SDK is handled automatically, you may still encounter conflict errors in the following situations:

Scenario Cause

Front-end interface and script edit the same picture at the same time The

frontend modified the graph, but SDK doesn’t know

Multiple scripts modify the same picture at the same time

's respective caches of timestamp conflict with each other

After opening the image for a long time, you continue to submit changes.

The graph has been updated by other operations and the cache has expired

What to do when you encounter conflict

The error is usually: 数据已修改，需要同步，请重新获取图 (see FAQ for details).

Solution (fixed routine):

  1. Recall open_graph() (main picture operation) or graph_node.open_graph() (sub picture operation)

  2. SDK automatically refreshes cache with new timestamp

  3. Continue with subsequent operations

# encounter timestamp Examples of handling conflicts
from atom_sdk import AtomClient, CreateNodeParams
from atom_sdk.core.errors import AtomApiError

client = AtomClient("http://127.0.0.1:10026")

try:
    result = client.node.create_node(CreateNodeParams("my_graph", "FilterNode"))
    print("Create node request status:", result["status"])
except AtomApiError as e:
    if "Data has been modified" in str(e) or "timestamp" in str(e).lower():
        # Resync
        client.graph.open_graph("my_graph")
        # Try again
        result = client.node.create_node(CreateNodeParams("my_graph", "FilterNode"))
        print("Retry request status:", result["status"])

Do I need to manually manage timestamp?

*Not required in most cases. *

Manual intervention may be required only in the following rare circumstances:

  • Your code waits a long time (several minutes or more) after the graph is opened before continuing.

  • You clearly know that the picture has been modified and want to refresh it actively

Manual refresh method:

# Manual refresh timestamp
client.graph.get_timestamp("my_graph")  # Equivalent to resync
# or
client.graph.open_graph("my_graph")    # Open the image and refresh at the same time

technical details

timestamp is a floating point number (Unix timestamp format), updated by the server on each modification. SDK’s TimestampStore are maintained in memory as dict[graph_name, float]. All Service of AtomClient share the same TimestampStore instance.
